facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and complete separation of the stratum corneum are consistent with peeling skin syndrome, which is supported by the 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene.

The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with keratosis pilaris.

The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and erythematous residual macules from previous erosions are consistent with ichthyosis.

The patient's mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, erythematous residual macules from previous erosions, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with atopic dermatitis.

The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and some lesions with unusual linear geographic contour are consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with erythrokeratodermia.
The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with Netherton syndrome.
The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with Darier disease.

The combination of skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and clean split just above the stratum granulosum, along with negative serological markers for celiac disease and normal immunofluorescence mapping results, points towards Peeling skin syndrome type B.

rationales.F02: Symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer may be related to environmental factors.
rationales.F05: Unusual linear geographic contour of lesions is a distinctive feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F09: Complete separation of the stratum corneum is a characteristic histopathological finding in peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F10: Clean split just above the stratum granulosum is a characteristic histopathological finding in peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F11: Heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome.
